newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters defends Morgan at news conference.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters defends Morgan at news conference.

text.p: New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Friday called a news conference to ask journalists to explain a story published in The National Business Review (NBR).

The story quoted an affidavit from a freelance journalist alleging NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan asked him to take photographs of him individually for use in his election campaign as part of a session at Maori broadcaster Aotearoa Television Netwrok (ATN) and bill the station.
Peters ruled out a by-election in Morgan's Te Tai Hauauru electorate after further allegations against Morgan in the media.
Asked if there would be a by-election (implying Morgan might resign) Peters said: "The question of by-elections is an absolute nonsense."
He said it was a beat-up by journalists matching each others' stories.

The photographer, Mark Walsh, said in his affidavit: "Before commencing to photograph Mr Morgan I asked him who would pay for these photographs. He made it clear to me the bill for his photographs was to be included in the account sent to ATN for the shoot I had done for them that day."

Walsh said he sent a bill to ATN for the session including for the roll of film used to shoot Morgan, but did not include the cost of the separate shoot for Morgan and he did not bill Morgan nor send him any photographs.
Morgan has been under attack since revelations he spent $4,000 of the station's money on clothing, including expensive underwear, two weeks before he was elected to parliament.
Morgan resigned as a director of ATN in July and was an employee of the station. He said he had authority to buy the clothes, but was contradicted by senior staff of the station.

"I want to know what it is in this story that merits the kind of attack on a member of parliament that I have seen this last week, and again in this article?" Peters asked press gallery journalists. No representative of NBR was present.
Peters said "to the best of my knowledge" the photos were not used in Morgan's campaign. He said Morgan only became a candidate in July and the photograph session was in March.
"Mr Morgan has given me a full briefing," Peters said, adding that the affidavit was not worth the paper it was written on.
"Mr Morgan has explained to me the photographs were part of a job lot with respect to ATN. He merely got the negatives and the negatives were never sent to him, they were sent to ATN."
Peters said Morgan had reimbursed ATN.
Morgan has refused to answer questions about the affair since parliament resumed on February 18.
